files.read_it.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
cur = con.cursor()

for name, price in cur.execute("SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC"):
    print(f"{name:<22}{price:>8.2f}")

con.close()
files.params.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
cur = con.cursor()

wanted = "USB-C hub"
cur.execute("SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE name = ?", (wanted,))
print("safe   ->", cur.fetchone())

evil = "' OR 1=1 --"
cur.execute(f"SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE name = '{evil}'")
rows = cur.fetchall()
print("unsafe ->", len(rows), "rows came back:")
for r in rows:
    print("          ", r)

con.close()
files.write_it.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
cur = con.cursor()

cur.execute("INSERT INTO products (name, price) VALUES (?, ?)", ("Webcam", 59.0))
print("new row id:", cur.lastrowid)

con.commit()
print("rows now:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products").fetchone()[0])

con.close()
files.row_factory.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row          # rows you can read by NAME
cur = con.cursor()

row = cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE id = 2").fetchone()
print("by index:", row[1])
print("by name :", row["name"], "costs", row["price"])
print("columns :", row.keys())

con.close()
files.many.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
cur = con.cursor()

new = [("Cable tidy", 9.0), ("Laptop stand", 42.0), ("Mouse mat", 12.5)]
cur.executemany("INSERT INTO products (name, price) VALUES (?, ?)", new)
print("inserted:", cur.rowcount, "rows in one call")

con.commit()
print("total now:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products").fetchone()[0])
con.close()
files.rollback.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("shop.db")
cur = con.cursor()

before = cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products").fetchone()[0]
cur.execute("DELETE FROM products")
print("after delete, this connection sees:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products").fetchone()[0])

con.rollback()
print("after rollback:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products").fetchone()[0], "(was", before, "before)")
con.close()
